about: Original content for Hue-drobe. The model (12 seasons, three traits) is the standard one; the questions, scoring numbers, wording and palettes are written for this app. Edit this file to change the quiz; no code change is needed unless the structure changes.

questions.text: Look at the inside of your wrist in daylight. What colour are your veins?
questions.help: Natural daylight by a window works best. Do not use a lamp.

answers.label: A mix, or I cannot tell

questions.text: Hold a silver item and a gold item against your bare face. Which looks better?
questions.help: A spoon, a ring or a piece of foil will do.

questions.text: How deep is your skin colour when it has not been tanned?
questions.help: Think of the skin on the inside of your upper arm.

questions.text: Which best describes the tone of your skin?

answers.label: Olive, or beige with a green or grey cast

questions.text: What is your natural hair colour?
questions.help: Ignore dye. If your hair has gone grey, pick the colour it was in your twenties.

questions.text: In sunlight, what do you see in your hair?

answers.label: A bit of both, or neither
Ash, grey-brown or blue-black, with no warm glints

questions.text: Which best describes your eye colour?

answers.label: Warm brown, amber or golden hazel
Soft grey, grey-green or muted hazel

questions.text: How do your eyes look up close?
questions.help: Look for how sharp the line is between the coloured part and the white.

answers.label: Bright and sharp: clear whites, a crisp edge to the colour
Soft and blended: the colour melts into the white

questions.text: Compare your hair, skin and eyes. How different are they from each other in depth?

answers.label: Strong contrast, such as dark hair with pale skin
Low contrast: all three are close in depth

questions.text: How does your skin react to the sun?

answers.label: It burns quickly and hardly ever tans
It freckles and burns, then turns golden
It tans easily to golden or bronze
It rarely burns and goes deeper

questions.text: A hint rather than a test: which kind of colour have people told you suits you?
questions.help: Skip to the middle answer if nobody has ever said.

seasons.name: Light Spring
seasons.description: Light, warm and delicate. Your colouring is fresh and gentle, with little depth and a touch of gold. Colours that are too heavy or too dark can sit on top of you rather than with you.

advice.flatters: Light, warm, clear colours such as peach, warm pink, buttercream, fresh leaf green and light aqua. Keep the depth low and the warmth gentle.
advice.neutrals: Ivory, cream, light camel, warm sand and soft warm grey. A light, clear navy works where others would wear black.
advice.careWith: Black, charcoal, stark white and very dark or dusty colours can overpower you. If you wear them, keep them away from your face.

seasons.name: True Spring
seasons.description: Warm, golden and lively. Warmth is your strongest trait, with colouring that is fairly clear and bright. You look best in colours that feel sunny and fresh.

advice.flatters: Warm, clear colours such as coral, poppy red, tangerine, sunny yellow, leaf green and turquoise.
advice.neutrals: Cream, golden tan, warm brown, camel and a warm navy. Choose these over black and grey.
advice.careWith: Cool, dusty or icy colours, such as grey-pink, slate and lavender grey, can make your skin look tired. Black is harsh near the face.

seasons.name: Bright Spring
seasons.description: Clear, vivid and a little warm. Your colouring has strong contrast and sparkle. Pure, saturated colours suit you; muted ones can make you look faded.

advice.flatters: Vivid, clean colours such as bright coral, sunshine yellow, emerald green, bright turquoise and clear blue. Strong colour pairings work well.
advice.neutrals: Warm white, clear navy, charcoal brown and a deep, warm grey. Avoid beige that is too soft.
advice.careWith: Dusty, greyed or earthy colours such as khaki, taupe and dull mauve. They flatten the contrast that makes you stand out.

seasons.name: Light Summer
seasons.description: Light, cool and soft-edged. Your colouring is gentle, with little depth and a cool, airy feel. Light colours with a hint of grey look natural on you.

advice.flatters: Light, cool colours such as soft pink, powder blue, lavender, pale mint and light rose.
advice.neutrals: Soft white, light grey, blue-grey, rose-beige and a soft navy. Mid grey can stand in for black.
advice.careWith: Black, orange, rust and very heavy, dark colours. They can swamp your colouring. Strong warm colours look out of place.

seasons.name: True Summer
seasons.description: Cool, soft and balanced. Coolness is your strongest trait, with colouring that is moderate in depth and gently muted. Cool colours with a little grey in them look best.

advice.flatters: Cool, slightly muted colours such as rose, dusty blue, periwinkle, blue-green and soft raspberry.
advice.neutrals: Cool grey, slate, blue-grey, cool navy and a soft white. Use grey-based browns rather than warm ones.
advice.careWith: Golden yellow, orange, tomato red and warm browns. They add a warmth you do not have and can make you look sallow.

seasons.name: Soft Summer
seasons.description: Muted, gentle and slightly cool. Your colouring blends together with low contrast. Greyed, smoky colours suit you, while very bright or very stark ones can look harsh.

advice.flatters: Soft, greyed colours such as dusty rose, misty blue, heather, grey-sage and mauve.
advice.neutrals: Stone, soft taupe, grey-brown, denim grey and charcoal blue. Use these in place of black or white.
advice.careWith: Neon or very bright colours, pure black and stark white. They can drown out your soft colouring.

seasons.name: Soft Autumn
seasons.description: Muted, earthy and slightly warm. Your colouring is gentle and blended, with a warm cast. Softened, natural colours suit you better than bold ones.

advice.flatters: Soft, warm, earthy colours such as terracotta, wheat, sage, muted jade, clay rose and moss.
advice.neutrals: Oatmeal, tan, soft cocoa, warm taupe and olive grey. Choose these rather than black or pure white.
advice.careWith: Neon, icy and very bright colours, and stark black. They fight your softness and make your skin look dull.

seasons.name: True Autumn
seasons.description: Warm, rich and earthy. Warmth is your strongest trait, with colouring that is medium to deep and a little muted. Colours that look like spices, leaves and gold suit you.

advice.flatters: Warm, rich colours such as rust, mustard, olive, deep teal, brick, pumpkin and fern green.
advice.neutrals: Cream, saddle brown, gold khaki, camel and dark olive. Brown usually does the job of black.
advice.careWith: Cool pastels, icy colours, blue-based pink and stark black or white. They can make your warm colouring look flat.

seasons.name: Deep Autumn
seasons.description: Deep, warm and rich. Your colouring has real depth, with a warm cast. Dark, saturated, earthy colours look natural on you, and pale ones can look washed out.

advice.flatters: Deep, warm colours such as dark brick, burnt copper, dark olive, deep teal, wine and antique gold.
advice.neutrals: Espresso, bronze, forest green, warm cream and dark chocolate. Warm black works if you want it.
advice.careWith: Pastels, icy colours and anything very light or cool. They lack the depth to hold their own against your colouring.

seasons.name: Deep Winter
seasons.description: Deep, cool and striking. Your colouring is dark with a cool cast and strong contrast. Dark, rich colours suit you well, while pale or warm ones can look weak.

advice.flatters: Deep, cool colours such as burgundy, deep blue, emerald, plum, deep raspberry and petrol.
advice.neutrals: Black, blue-black, charcoal, cool slate and icy white. Black is usually safe for you.
advice.careWith: Soft pastels, dusty colours and warm shades such as orange and mustard. They lack the depth and coolness your colouring needs.

seasons.name: True Winter
seasons.description: Cool, clear and high in contrast. Coolness is your strongest trait. Pure, cool colours and sharp contrasts, such as black with white, look good on you.

advice.flatters: Cool, clear colours such as true red, royal blue, emerald, royal purple, cool pink and icy tones.
advice.neutrals: Black, navy, pure white, cool grey and silver grey. Strong contrast between light and dark works well.
advice.careWith: Warm, earthy or muted colours such as mustard, rust, khaki and peach. They look dull against your cool colouring.

seasons.name: Bright Winter
seasons.description: Vivid, cool and sharp. Your colouring is clear and high in contrast, with a cool lean. Intense, electric colours suit you, while muted ones can make you look faded.

advice.flatters: Vivid, cool colours such as vivid raspberry, electric blue, jade, vivid violet, hot pink and cherry red.
advice.neutrals: Ink black, optic white, charcoal and a clear, dark navy. Icy tints are good for lighter pieces.
advice.careWith: Muted, dusty or earthy colours such as khaki, beige and soft taupe. They dim the clarity that makes your colouring striking.
